frequencies.timing_details: Take once every 24 hours at approximately the same time each day.
frequencies.ismp_status: Acceptable in UK/Commonwealth; in USA, ISMP recommends writing 'daily' to avoid confusion with 'OS' (left eye) or 'OD' (right eye).
frequencies.verified_source: British National Formulary (BNF) / Latin Sig Codes

frequencies.timing_details: Take once daily.
frequencies.ismp_status: PROHIBITED on ISMP and Joint Commission Do Not Use lists. Often misread as QID (four times daily). Always write 'daily'.
frequencies.verified_source: The Joint Commission Official Do Not Use List / ISMP

frequencies.timing_details: Take twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart (typically morning and evening).
frequencies.ismp_status: Standard international abbreviation. Ensure clear spacing.

frequencies.timing_details: Take two times a day, approximately 10 to 12 hours apart (e.g. 8 AM and 8 PM).
Take three times daily during waking hours, roughly 6 to 8 hours apart (e.g. morning, afternoon, evening).

frequencies.english: Three times a day to be taken
frequencies.timing_details: Take three times daily (morning, midday, night).
frequencies.ismp_status: Commonly used in UK, Commonwealth, and India.

frequencies.timing_details: Take four times daily, spaced evenly throughout the day (approximately every 4 to 6 hours while awake).
frequencies.ismp_status: Standard. Ensure not confused with QD.

frequencies.english: Four times a day to be taken
frequencies.timing_details: Take four times daily.
Take around the clock every 4 hours (e.g. 6 times per 24 hours).
Take around the clock every 6 hours (e.g. 4 times per 24 hours).
Take every 8 hours (e.g. 3 times per 24 hours, evenly spaced).
Take every 12 hours (e.g. 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM).
Take once nightly right before going to sleep.
frequencies.ismp_status: ISMP cautions against 'qhs' as 'hs' can mean half-strength. Recommended to write 'at bedtime'.

frequencies.timing_details: Take at sleep time.
frequencies.ismp_status: Write 'at bedtime' to avoid mistaking for 'half strength'.

frequencies.timing_details: Take only when required for specified symptom (e.g. pain, fever, nausea). Respect the minimum interval specified (e.g. 'PRN pain Q6H max 3 tabs/day').
frequencies.ismp_status: Must always be paired with a clinical indication (e.g. PRN pain, PRN fever) and maximum daily limit.

frequencies.english: If necessary / In case of emergency
frequencies.timing_details: Take a single dose if needed. In Commonwealth/Indian prescriptions, often used identically to PRN (e.g. Tab Paracetamol SOS).
Administer right away as a single emergency or loading dose.
Administered once every week (e.g. once every 7 days).
Administered two times each week at regular intervals.
Administered three times each week (e.g. Mon-Wed-Fri).
Administered every alternate day.
frequencies.ismp_status: ISMP cautions against 'qod'; write 'every other day'.

food_timings.english: Before meals / On an empty stomach
food_timings.instruction: Take 30 to 60 minutes before eating food or drinking anything other than water.
food_timings.clinical_rationale: Prevents food from blocking drug absorption or, for proton pump inhibitors, allows the drug to block acid pumps before they are activated by a meal.

food_timings.instruction: Take immediately or within 30 minutes after completing a meal.
food_timings.clinical_rationale: Food buffers gastric mucosa against irritation/ulcers (NSAIDs), or enhances drug absorption, or reduces gastrointestinal upset/nausea.

food_timings.instruction: Take midway through your meal or with the first few bites of food.
food_timings.clinical_rationale: Ensures direct mixing with food to maximize absorption of fat-soluble agents or reduce direct mucosal contact.
common_examples: Atorvastatin (can take with or without food)

food_timings.instruction: Take at least 1 hour before eating or 2 hours after your last meal, with a full glass of plain water.
food_timings.clinical_rationale: Food components (such as dietary calcium, proteins, or fats) severely bind or degrade the active compound.

routes.english: Injected into fatty tissue under skin (e.g. insulin)
Inhaled through the mouth into lungs
Inhaled as a fine mist via nebulizer machine
